summary.text: CA9 is a leading antigen/imaging and biomarker hypothesis. Its computed convergence rank is [gene=CA9; type=analysis_ranking; source=ANALYSIS:ranking:convergence:8d5ff79b77e8d233; profile=convergence; rank=1]. Expression and sampled cell-attribution evidence support follow-up, and girentuximab has a clinical-development record in the frozen snapshot. Missing confirmatory protein testing, normal-tissue staining and lack of selective dependency limit the interpretation; this is not a treatment recommendation.

NNMT combines expression, confirmatory protein and literature evidence with an overall-survival association: [gene=NNMT; type=tcga_survival; source=DATASET:TCGA-KIRC-RNA; log_hr_per_sd=0.301] [gene=NNMT; type=tcga_survival; source=DATASET:TCGA-KIRC-RNA; padj=0.0048]. It remains a biomarker and functional-intervention hypothesis. The available cell-line dependency result does not establish selective dependence, and preclinical inhibitor findings are not clinical efficacy evidence.

CD70 has expression and antibody-development evidence, but its sampled cell of origin differs across cohorts. Its immune-cell transcript share is [gene=CD70; type=immune_profile; source=CPTAC CIBERSORT and xCell immune deconvolution; immune_cell_share_of_tumour_transcripts=0.654]. Missing vital-organ staining prevents a safety conclusion. It should not be presented as an established tumour-cell-restricted target.

The rankings address different questions. Expression-loss genes such as PSAT1 and PCK1 motivate biomarker studies. EPAS1 supplies an established drug-development reference but has context-dependent expression and dependency evidence. None of these observations alone establishes which intervention will benefit an individual patient.

PSAT1, PCK1, ALDH6A1, ALDOB and SLC22A8 represent expression-loss candidates. A tumour-versus-normal decrease and a within-tumour survival association answer different questions. They do not by themselves justify inhibiting the depleted protein.

literature.text: CA9 imaging and CD70 targeting papers provide study-specific support, with prospective or functional validation still required. Their abstract-level claims do not override discordant cell attribution or missing normal-tissue measurements.

NNMT inhibitor studies include renal cancer cell-line experiments and experimental intervention findings. SLC16A3 literature proposes an immune-metabolic mechanism. A non-selective dependency result cannot prove that any therapeutic effect must operate exclusively through the microenvironment.

The full PSAT1 abstract describes reduced RNA and protein expression in ccRCC. Its pathway-enrichment statement is a different comparison, so the earlier claim of contradictory expression evidence is withdrawn. Functional intervention in that paper concerns HPGD. Absence of an extracted relation for other candidates is not absence of literature.

external.text: CA9, CD70 and ENPP3 have named clinical-development records in the frozen Open Targets snapshot. A target-level drug stage is not proof of a ccRCC indication, accessibility or efficacy. Compounds and their citations are individually identified in the detailed external findings.

VHL mutation observations: [gene=VHL; type=somatic_recurrence; source=DATASET:SOMATIC-CPTAC-TCGA; mutated_patients=247] among [gene=VHL; type=somatic_recurrence; source=DATASET:SOMATIC-CPTAC-TCGA; patients=511]. This is disease-mechanism evidence, not evidence that inhibiting VHL would be beneficial. The EPAS1 drug record should be interpreted separately from expression-based candidate rankings.

cells.text: CA9 and NNMT have concordant dominant RCC-cell attribution across the two sampled single-cell cohorts. This does not establish exclusivity across all tissues.
CD70 and SLC16A3 have discordant dominant-cell assignments between cohorts. Reproducible bulk expression increases do not resolve that attribution conflict.

EPAS1 and KDR show substantial endothelial attribution in the sampled tissue; CD74 and CXCR4 show immune-cell contributions. MET has a predominantly RCC-cell transcript share. Cell abundance and per-cell expression must be considered together.

validation.text: External RNA replication supports expression reproducibility for the leading tumour-up candidates. Purity extrapolation remains model-dependent and cannot establish that a bulk signal is free of infiltration. Survival associations need independent prognostic validation.

NNMT, SCARB1, PSAT1 and PCK1 satisfy the stated confirmatory protein replication criterion. CA9 and CD70 lack adequate matched-pair protein testing here, which is missing evidence rather than failed replication. PCK1 and PSAT1 differ in phosphosite replication; those counts are shown in the detailed applied findings.

EPAS1 meets the configured selective-dependency rule with selectivity [gene=EPAS1; type=depmap_dependency; source=DATASET:DEPMAP-26Q1; selectivity=0.3] and adjusted p-value [gene=EPAS1; type=depmap_dependency; source=DATASET:DEPMAP-26Q1; padj=0.0609]. This depends on the configured threshold and is above the conventional adjusted significance threshold. The expression-ranked candidates lack a comparable selective-dependency result; expression is not a substitute for functional evidence.

treatment.text: The reviewed treatment estimates for CA9, CD70 and PCK1 do not pass their adjusted association tests or establish predictive arm differences. Their signs are point estimates, not demonstrated treatment benefit. NNMT has only the small nivolumab-cohort result in the available record; missing IMmotion150 values are not negative results. Failure to detect a difference is not proof of equivalence.

subtypes.text: CA9 has a PBRM1 subgroup flag supported primarily by RNA; its corresponding protein comparison is not significant under the stated criterion. PSAT1 has measurable ccB-versus-ccA differences. NNMT nonsignificance does not establish a uniform pan-subtype marker. Full driver/cohort comparisons, including discordance, appear in the applied findings.

adc.text: CD70 lacks vital-organ staining evidence. CA9, ENPP3 and SCARB1 show normal-tissue staining that requires attention; SCARB1 also has sparse sampled tumour-cell coverage. SLC16A3 combines a high heuristic suitability score with multipass topology and limited extracellular sequence. None of these scores establishes antibody accessibility, internalisation, toxicity or conjugate efficacy.

immune.text: FCGR3A and CD70 have substantial immune-cell transcript contributions, while CD74 and CXCR4 support immune-compartment attribution. Deconvolution correlation is not causal proof of infiltration. Concordant CA9 and NNMT cell attribution is limited to the sampled cohorts.

integration.text: Keep modality hypotheses separate. Antigen-directed proposals need accessibility and normal-tissue evidence; enzyme or transporter inhibition needs functional intervention evidence; biomarker proposals need diagnostic, prognostic or predictive validation appropriate to their intended use. A cavity or exposed loop cannot promote a candidate to an MGD mechanism. Missing evidence, non-favorable measurements and cross-cohort contradictions remain distinct in the candidate cards.

limitations.text: No failures detected by automatic checks is not complete scientific validation. Linkage, numeric bindings and limited direction rules cannot prove every interpretation.
The post-2016 clinical-target evaluation is retrospective: inputs contain information published after the cutoff and are not a prospectively frozen feature set.
Observational expression, survival and treatment associations are not causal or therapeutic efficacy evidence. Nonsignificance does not establish equivalence.
The abstract corpus and external-source snapshots are bounded and incomplete. Absence of a retrieved record is not absence of biology or literature.
Monomer structural context is not a degron or MGD predictor. Experimental references cannot be transferred to other proteins, ligases, compounds or isoforms without evidence.
Technical replication, source versions, normal-tissue coverage and model confidence each impose distinct limitations. See the candidate evidence cards and source records.
